name: TV stand or media console
tagline: A long cam-lock box with doors, cable holes, and a top that has to carry your television.
peopleNote: One to build. Two to lift the finished unit and definitely two to put the TV on it.

tools.why: Squaring the box and centring the doors.
Adjusting hinge screws so the doors line up. This is what makes it look professional.

before: Measure the TV's feet, not its screen size. A 65-inch TV with wide-set feet needs a stand wider than most people expect.
Build it where it will live. A six-foot console does not turn a corner in a hallway.
Check the stand's weight rating against your TV. It is on the listing or in the manual.
safety: A TV on a stand can be pulled over by a child. Use the stand's anti-tip strap and also strap the TV itself to the wall or the stand.
Never put a TV on a unit whose cams are not fully locked and whose back panel is not nailed on.

steps.title: Spread out and label everything
steps.say: Media consoles have the most look-alike panels of any furniture. Lay them all out, match each to its letter in the manual, and pencil the letter on.
do: All panels out, none stacked
Match every one to the parts diagram
Pencil the letter on a hidden face
steps.watch: Long horizontal panels for the top, bottom and shelves often differ by a quarter inch. Labeling is not optional here.

steps.title: Dowels and cam bolts in
steps.say: Tap the dowels halfway into the edge holes and hand-tighten the cam bolts into the face holes, exactly as the diagram shows for each panel.
do: Dowels in edge holes, half in
Cam bolts in face holes, hand-tight to the shoulder
Do all panels before you join any
steps.tip: Doing all the prep across every panel first, then all the joining, is much faster than panel-by-panel.

steps.title: Cams into the big holes, gap toward the joint
steps.say: Each big round hole takes a cam lock, with the keyhole gap pointing toward the edge the bolt arrives from. Check every one before you close anything.
do: One cam per large round hole
Keyhole gap faces the incoming bolt
Flush with the surface
steps.watch: On a unit this size you may be inserting twenty cams. One backwards means one joint that never closes, and finding it later is miserable.

steps.title: Build the two end sections first
steps.say: Most consoles are really two small boxes joined by a long top and bottom. Build each end section flat first, then bring them together.
do: Side panel flat, divider and shelves in
Lock those cams
Repeat for the other end
steps.tip: Two small assemblies joined at the end is far easier to handle than wrestling a six-foot frame from the start.

steps.title: Join with the top and bottom, then lock
steps.say: Lay the long bottom down, stand both end sections on it, then set the top across. Get every dowel started before you press anything home.
do: Bottom panel down first
End sections on, dowels started
Top across, press down evenly along its whole length
steps.watch: Pressing one end fully home before the other starts cracks dowel holes. Work along the length evenly.

steps.title: Square it, then fit the back
steps.say: Measure both diagonals and push until they match. Then fit the back panel, which locks that shape in and gives you your cable holes.
do: Diagonals equal
Back panel printed side out
Corner nails first, then all the way round and into the dividers
steps.tip: Punch out or locate the cable holes in the back before nailing it on. Doing it afterwards means working in a tiny gap.
steps.watch: Doors will never line up on an out-of-square box. This step is why some consoles look factory-made and others look homemade.

steps.title: Hang the doors and adjust the hinges
steps.say: Screw the hinge plates into the cabinet, clip the doors on, then use the hinge adjustment screws to line the doors up with each other.
do: Hinge plates into the pre-drilled cup holes in the cabinet
Clip or screw the door hinges to the plates
Adjust: one screw moves the door sideways, one moves it in and out, one moves it up and down
steps.tip: Close both doors and look at the gap between them. Turn the adjustment screws a quarter turn at a time until that gap is even top to bottom. Five minutes of this transforms how the whole thing looks.
steps.watch: Hinges are handed on some units. If a door hangs at a strange angle, you may have a left hinge on the right door.

steps.title: Handles, shelf pins, and the inside
steps.say: Bolt the handles through the pre-drilled holes, push in the shelf pins at matching heights, and drop in the adjustable shelves.
do: Handle bolts go in from the inside of the door
Shelf pins: count holes from the bottom, same count all four corners
Shelves in, press each corner
steps.tip: If a handle bolt is too long and sticks out, add a washer or two behind the handle to take up the slack.

steps.title: Sort the cables while the back is still accessible
steps.say: Set up the console, box, and power strip now and feed everything through the cable holes before the TV is on top blocking your view.
do: Power strip inside the cabinet, or screwed to the back
Each device's cable through its own hole
Label both ends of every cable with masking tape
steps.tip: Labeling cables with masking tape and a pen takes two minutes and saves an hour every single time you change anything.

steps.title: TV on, then strap everything down
steps.say: With two people, lift the TV on and center it. Then strap the console to the wall and strap the TV to the console or the wall.
do: Two people, lift from the bottom bezel and the back, never the screen
Center it over the unit's vertical dividers if you can
Anti-tip strap on the console, anti-tip strap or wall mount on the TV
steps.tip: Put the TV's weight over a vertical divider rather than the unsupported middle of a long top panel.
steps.watch: Tipping televisions injure thousands of children a year, nearly always off a chest or a stand. Both straps, every time.

fixes.q: The doors do not line up and the gap is crooked
fixes.a: This is what hinge adjustment screws are for, and it is almost never a manufacturing fault. Close both doors, find the uneven gap, and turn the sideways-adjustment screw on the offending hinge a quarter turn at a time. Also confirm the cabinet is square.

fixes.q: The top sags in the middle under the TV
fixes.a: The TV's weight is over an unsupported span. Shift the TV so its feet sit over the vertical dividers, or add a support block or a center leg underneath.

fixes.q: A door hangs open or swings shut by itself
fixes.a: The whole unit is not level. Adjust the feet or shim the low side — doors are a very sensitive level gauge.

fixes.q: The cable holes are in the wrong places for my setup
fixes.a: Most back panels are thin hardboard. A new hole can be cut with a hole saw or even a sharp knife, from the inside out, with the panel supported. Mark it first and keep it away from the edges.

fixes.q: My TV is wider than the stand
fixes.a: Overhang up to a few inches each side is usually fine structurally but looks wrong and is easy to knock. Check the TV's foot spacing against the stand's top width — feet must land fully on the surface.
